text: An API key is a hot wallet. On 16 November 2026 one wallet withdrew about 10.39 million USDC from Lighter's contract (Bitquery on-chain trace); Lighter said a leaked API key for one trader's account caused it and that its protocol and smart contracts were unaffected. Lighter's postmortem said a trader's custom signing software reused nonces so the key could be computed from public signatures, and the attacker moved the victim's funds into a public pool and redeemed them. Lighter's Security Council returned about $5 million, withdrawals were later restored, wallet signature requirements were added for public-pool transfers, and IP allowlists and configurable API key permissions are planned. A Lighter API key can trade, cancel, modify, change leverage, manage sub-accounts and withdraw to its own L1 address. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-18)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: Paradex's RPI order type is not accessible to standard API traders: retail taker orders (JWT with token_usage=interactive) get a 300ms speed bump and rate limits 267-575x lower than standard API limits. The API order book does not contain RPI orders. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: A taker-side delay is a transfer, not a free lunch, and who ends up paying depends on maker competition. Multicoin: delay-based methods do not eliminate toxic order flow but determine where it appears and who pays, and toxic flow raises spreads for everyone. Baldauf and Mollner (CEPR VoxEU): delaying non-cancellation orders improves conditions for liquidity providers, and competition among them will likely pass some or all of the gain to other traders as tighter, deeper quotes. This is a model prediction, not a measured result for Lighter. (medium confidence)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: Moving money is not free even when trading is. Variational charges a flat $0.1 per deposit or withdrawal. On Lighter, account-to-account transfers and fast withdrawals use the transferFeeInfo endpoint, and the fee is charged on top of the amount. A fast withdrawal is USDC-only with a 4 USDC minimum, while a secure withdrawal goes only to the owner's own L1 address and settles via Ethereum. DefiLlama lists transfer and withdrawal fees among Lighter's protocol revenue. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: On Lighter the zero fee is paid for in latency: Standard accounts have 300 ms taker latency and 300 ms cancel/modify latency, with 0 ms maker latency. An API user who wants speed must opt into Premium/Advanced, which has 140 ms taker latency and 0 ms maker/cancel but charges 0.0040% maker / 0.0280% taker at the base (0 staked LIT) tier. Plus accounts cost 0.5bps and keep 300 ms taker latency; they raise rate limits. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: Liquidation is a separate cost wedge on zero-fee venues. Lighter's liquidation engine takes up to a 1% liquidation fee, paid to the LLP insurance fund, when an IoC liquidation fills better than the zero price; Variational force-liquidates at ask +0.5% (short) or bid -0.5% (long). Both venues therefore charge an exit cost on failed positions even with zero trading fees. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: Lighter's LLP vault, which provides a large share of liquidity at the top of the book, drew down about 5.35% in the October 2025 $20B crypto crash while Hyperliquid's HLP generated over $40 million in profit. Lighter announced a compensation plan for affected LLP holders. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-10-14)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: Fee-free retail pricing is paid for by flow segmentation: venues give retail a speed bump or private liquidity so makers can quote tighter, and charge latency-sensitive or API flow either explicit fees (Lighter Premium 0.0280% taker) or delay (Lighter 300ms). (medium confidence)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: Lighter's zero fee covers only regular perp and spot orders on the default Standard account; Standard pays 1 bp on TWAP/advanced orders and RFQ. Opt-in mainnet tiers charge: Plus 0.5bps maker and taker (300 ms taker latency), and Premium/Advanced 0.0040% maker / 0.0280% taker at zero staked LIT (140 ms taker latency), falling to 0.0028% / 0.0196% at 500,000 staked LIT. The API user who wants speed therefore pays on Lighter; the zero is for latency-insensitive Standard flow. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: On a Lighter Standard account the zero fee is paid for in time: taker orders and cancel/modify requests wait a 300 ms speed bump while maker (post-only) orders wait 0 ms; Premium cancels and post-only orders add no latency and taker latency is 140 ms. Lighter's developer docs add that every transaction waits in a per-API-key queue, so a post-only order sent right after a taker order on the same key waits the taker's 300 ms; Premium accounts can mark keys maker-only to skip the queue, and the docs advise one key per workload. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: Fee-free retail pricing is financed by flow segmentation plus explicit fees on the segment that is expensive to serve. Paradex charges makers 0.5 bps and Pro/API takers 0.0175% to 0.045% while Retail pays 0%; Lighter charges Plus and Premium accounts; Variational keeps the spread. A taker-signal bot on an API key should expect to be classed with the paying or delayed segment. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: Paradex's own fee-drag comparison (April 2, 2026) models fees only: ten BTC scalps at 50× leverage with Binance regular 0.02%/0.05% fees (net $8.50) against Paradex Retail 0% (net $58.50). It acknowledges that funding matters too and that API traders pay a tiered rate, but it does not model the Retail API cap of 1,000 orders per 24 hours or the 300ms speed bump. Vendor fee-drag math is a headline-fee comparison, not an all-in cost. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: API throughput is an economic constraint. Lighter Standard accounts are limited to 60 requests per minute, 250 active and 50 pending orders per account. Plus and Premium get 4000 or more sendTx per minute, but creating, modifying or cancel-all orders consume volume quota earned at 1 quota per $1-$2 of fill notional (BTC, ETH and SOL at the $2 default), plus one free sendTx every 15 s; single-order cancels are free. Paradex Retail API orders are capped at 1,000 per 24 hours and Pro at 17,250 per minute. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: Lighter's account-types, rate-limits and volume-quota pages each hold two network schedules: mainnet (mainnet.zklighter.elliot.ai) and Lighter on Robinhood Chain (api.rh.lighter.xyz). The Robinhood Chain Premium tier is volume-tiered (below $1M volume: 0.0120% maker, 0.0350% taker, 200 ms taker latency; above $500M: 0.0084% / 0.0245%, 150 ms), Plus is 0.015% with 200 ms maker/cancel latency, and Standard maker/cancel latency is 200 ms. Mainnet Premium is LIT-staking tiered. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: Variational Omni charges no trading fee. The Omni Liquidity Provider (OLP) is the counterparty to all trades on Omni, determines a fair spread for each asset, and hedges the directional exposure it accumulates through external venues; the protocol currently takes 20% of the spreads paid to OLP (a rate the docs say is still being tested and may change). The user's cost is the spread, not a fee. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: Exit and liquidation costs survive a zero trading fee. Lighter's liquidation engine takes up to a 1% fee, paid to the LLP insurance fund, when an IoC liquidation fills better than the zero price; Variational force-liquidates at ask +0.5% (short) or bid -0.5% (long) and charges a flat $0.1 per deposit or withdrawal; Paradex charges a 0.015% settlement fee on positions open at delisting; Lighter limits L2Withdraw to 2 requests per minute and 3 requests per 2 hours. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: Funding is the cost zero fees do not touch. Castle Labs (September 2026 data snapshot): BTC funding ran 1.9% to 7.6% a year on every venue, Lighter's WTI funding reached +95% a year for longs, and an OpenAI pre-IPO long cost about 33% a year while QFEX paid about 1%. Lighter charges hourly funding with a market-specific premium multiplier (1 for crypto, 1/2 for RWA, 1/100 for pre-IPO). Paradex says the only frictions left are spread and funding. Variational claims perp funding spiked past 80% annualized in an early-November Nasdaq selloff while swap funding stayed around 5% (a company claim). OpenChainBench excludes funding. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: Hyperliquid is the baseline a zero-fee venue is measured against: base perp fees are 0.045% taker and 0.015% maker, falling with trailing volume to 0.024% taker and 0.000% maker above $7B, with up to 40% HYPE-staking discount and maker rebates of -0.001% to -0.003% for maker volume shares above 0.5% to 3.0%. Castle Labs reports realised take rates of 2.6 bps for Hyperliquid and 0.8 bps for Lighter. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: Lighter funds its zero-fee retail tier from other payers and from liquidations. Standard accounts pay no fee on regular perp and spot orders but 1 bp on TWAP/advanced orders and RFQ. Plus accounts pay 0.5bps. Premium/Advanced accounts pay 0.0040% maker and 0.0280% taker before LIT-staking discounts. Liquidations carry a per-market fee, currently 1%, that goes to LLP. DefiLlama splits Lighter's fees into protocol revenue (maker, taker, transfer and withdrawal fees) and supply-side revenue, which its methodology defines as liquidation fees paid to LLP. On-Chain Times likewise attributed Lighter revenue to the 1% liquidation fee plus Premium traders' fees. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: Two independent measurements rank Lighter's Standard tier cheapest to open on majors at small and mid sizes. OpenChainBench reads venue APIs and defines cost as taker fee plus half-spread plus book impact for a $1000 long. It showed Lighter at 0.0036% all-in (ETH 0.0036%, BTC 0.0033%, SOL 0.0033%). Paradex's Retail book was 0.031%, Hyperliquid 0.048% and Aster 0.051%. Castle Labs measured 0.41 bps to open a $100k BTC position on Lighter against 4.71 bps on Hyperliquid, using order-book data of 23 September 2026. Neither cost definition includes the Standard tier's 300 ms taker delay, or funding. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: Paradex says it earns from RPI maker flow, not from retail takers. Professional makers post RPI orders that are visible in the UI and hidden from the API. These match only against Retail takers, and the makers pay 0.5 bps on RPI fills; the Pro maker fee in the current docs is a flat 0.005%. Paradex calls the model analogous to TradFi payment for order flow (PFOF). An SEC DERA staff working paper (January 2025) measured PFOF rates of about 35 bps in crypto markets, against 8 bps for options and 0.8 bps for equities in prior work, and attributes the premium to crypto order flow being highly uninformed. Multicoin gives the same logic: makers lose to informed flow and earn the spread on uninformed flow. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: TradFi evidence shows a zero commission can hide an execution-price cost that no fee page reveals. Schwarz et al. sent 85,000 simultaneous market orders through six accounts at five brokers. Mean account-level round-trip cost ranged from -0.07% to -0.46% excluding commissions, because off-exchange wholesalers gave different execution prices to different brokers. Variation in PFOF did not explain the dispersion. This is an equity analogue, not perp data. (low confidence)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: Oak Research reports, citing Variational's published reports, that 43% to 78% of Omni's gross revenue (about 57% on average) goes to market-making and hedging costs, and the rest is split between OLP depositors, the treasury and referral rewards. Oak also flags the single team-run counterparty as a point of centralization and opacity, and says price quality depends on the oracle and on aggregated external liquidity. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: Reported volume on points-driven zero-fee venues is a weak measure of real activity. Volume-to-open-interest turnover for Lighter was 8.03, against 1.57 for Hyperliquid, 5.4 for Aster and 2.7 for EdgeX (Stacy Muur). Castle Labs measured 2.87x a day for Lighter against 1.16x for Hyperliquid in its data for 17 August to 15 September 2026, and 7x to 9x for Jupiter Perps, Pacifica and GMTrade. Formo, using a DefiLlama snapshot of November 8, 2026, computed about 3.6x for Lighter, 2.6x for Variational and 1.1x for Hyperliquid and Aster. Formo says a high ratio is not proof of wash trading because venue design and fees differ. The open-source delta-farmer bot automates hedged volume creation for points programs on Lighter, Variational's Omni, Pacifica and other venues. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-08)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: Zero is measured against Hyperliquid's schedule. Hyperliquid's base perp rate is 0.045% taker and 0.015% maker. It falls with trailing volume to 0.024% taker and 0.000% maker above $7B. HYPE-staking tiers cut fees by up to 40% (above 500,000 HYPE staked), and maker rebates of -0.001% to -0.003% go to the largest maker-volume shares. TrueHold computes a $10,000 market-order round trip at $9 on Hyperliquid's base tier, $5.60 on Lighter Premium before discounts and $0 on Lighter Standard. Compare any zero-fee venue with the fee tier you would really hold, not the base rate. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: Variational's economics are reported (BlockBeats) as a 4-6 bp spread charged to users against 0-2 bp hedging cost, with OLP annualised returns above 300% in Apr-Jul 2025. The article says hedging cost could exceed spread income in extreme market conditions, and that Variational uses a last-look rejection mechanism as a risk control. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-09-11)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: Funding and index risk remain even when fees are zero. In Castle Labs' Sept 2026 data snapshot BTC funding ran 1.9% to 7.6% a year on every venue, Lighter's WTI funding reached +95% a year for longs on weekends, venue indices diverged by up to 30 bps on weekends, and pre-IPO perps (Anthropic, OpenAI) differed across venues by 379 and 569 bps. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-01)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: On Lighter, speed and throughput are the paid features, and the zero fee is paid for with latency. Standard accounts have 300 ms taker and cancel/modify latency and no maker latency. Premium/Advanced has 140 ms taker latency at 0.004% maker and 0.028% taker, with up to 30% off for 500,000 staked LIT. Plus costs 0.5bps, keeps the 300 ms taker delay, and raises rate limits. LIT fee credits count toward both the fee-discount tier and the rate-limit tier, and their proceeds go to stakers. TrueHold says 300 ms of slippage can exceed the 0.028% taker fee for frequent liquidity takers in fast markets. Cartea et al. model why: during a delay the book can update, so a marketable order may miss its fill or fill at a worse price. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: Lighter's LLP is the backstop behind zero-fee trading, so liquidity providers absorb the shock. LLP is the counterparty to all LLP trading and liquidations. ADL starts only when LLP, or the relevant LLP strategy, cannot cover losses. LLP strategies segregate collateral by market group (for example crypto perps, FX, equities/RWA), so losses stay inside one strategy. LLP is open only to LIT stakers, up to 10 USDC deposited per 1 LIT staked. On-Chain Times reported that larger outside market makers had cut LLP's maker share from about 80% to about 7%. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: Variational's Omni charges no trading fees and keeps the spread, with its Omni Liquidity Provider (OLP) acting as the only maker; the protocol takes a cut of Omni's spread revenue rather than a cut of fees. (high confidence)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: Zero trading fee does not mean zero execution cost on Variational: the docs list a flat $0.1 per deposit/withdrawal, and a liquidation penalty by force-liquidating at ask +0.5% (short) or bid -0.5% (long). Castle Labs adds that Variational swaps charge a daily carry fee instead of funding. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: Castle Labs measured Lighter's cost to open a $100k BTC position at 0.41 bps (slippage plus standard taker fee, zero on Standard) versus 4.71 bps on Hyperliquid, and reported Lighter over 60% cheaper than the centralised median; Castle states a 5 bps taker fee on a $100K BTC order costs $50, about 75x the slippage. Castle reports take rate of 0.8 bps on Lighter vs 2.6 bps on Hyperliquid. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-01)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: Reported volume on zero-fee and points-driven venues is a weak liquidity signal. Castle Labs reports Jupiter Perps, Pacifica and GMTrade turning over 7x to 9x open interest daily (vs Hyperliquid 1.16x, Lighter 2.87x), consistent with points programs and airdrop farming; an earlier analyst note put Lighter's closed-beta volume/OI ratio near 27 and suggested wash trading or incentive-driven activity. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-01)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: Castle Labs measured a take rate of 0.8 bps for Lighter vs 2.6 bps for Hyperliquid (DefiLlama fee and volume series, 17 Aug-15 Sep 2026), despite no fee on Standard accounts. On-Chain Times put revenue near $500k a day on more than $10b in trading volume most days (a community estimate; Lighter had not published exact revenue), attributed to the 1% liquidation fee and Premium users' trading fees, with the LLP vault receiving most of the exchange's revenue. ChainCatcher cites DefiLlama monthly revenue of $10.27 million on $227.19 billion of 30-day volume. Lighter's docs confirm the liquidation engine takes up to a 1% fee into the LLP insurance fund. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-15)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: On Castle Labs' static order-book walk (23 September 2026), the cost to open a $100,000 position on Lighter's Standard account was 0.41 bps BTC, 0.83 ETH, 1.73 SOL, 2.53 ZEC and 2.20 HYPE, versus Hyperliquid 4.71 / 4.82 / 5.56 / 6.87 / 6.93 and the Binance-Bybit-OKX median 5.07 / 5.10 / 6.07 / 9.06 / 8.24. Lighter's slippage alone was higher than Hyperliquid's and the CEX median on BTC (0.41 vs 0.21 vs 0.07 bps), so the missing taker fee, not tighter books, makes it cheapest. OpenChainBench's independent live benchmark agrees at $1000: Lighter 0.0036% all-in on ETH vs 0.048% for Hyperliquid and the lowest of 11 ranked venues (2026-11-22). (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: Size changes the ranking. A taker fee is a flat rate while price impact grows with size. OpenChainBench notes that at $1,000,000 of notional the price impact dwarfs the taker fee, so a zero fee venue can lose to a 4 bps venue whose book absorbs the size; Castle Labs found Hyperliquid had the lowest median slippage at $1M of five venues (3.7 bps vs 3.8 on Binance) yet Lighter stayed over 60% cheaper than the centralised median after fees. Castle's 7-day median to 22 November 2026 shows Lighter BTC slippage of 0.65 bps at $100k and 1.7 bps at $1M, with $11.9M of depth within 0.1% versus $33.5M on OKX. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: Variational's spread cost is reported inconsistently, and the numbers measure different things. BlockBeats reports a 4-6 bps spread charged to users against 0-2 bps hedging cost; Alea Research (via Bankless) estimates Q3 spreads at 2.35 bps of volume against 2.40 bps in average perp fees on Hyperliquid, partly from the team's own disclosures; Castle Labs measured a 4.66 bps median quoted spread across seven TradFi perps in US hours and a 2.82 bps cost to open $100k, versus 1.04 bps for Lighter and 2.90 for TradeXYZ, and did not test Variational on crypto. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: Zero-fee order books push adverse-selection risk onto the liquidity vault. In the October 2025 crash Lighter's LLP drew down about 5.35% (On-Chain Times: about 5%) while Hyperliquid's HLP made over $40 million; Lighter prioritised giving users liquidity instead of ADL, and LLP holders were compensated in points (On-Chain Times). LLP's maker market share had fallen from about 80% to about 7%, leaving it a liquidity backstop earning most of the exchange's revenue. (high confidence)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: Reported volume on points-driven zero-fee venues is a weak liquidity signal. Castle Labs (17 Aug-15 Sep 2026): daily volume over open interest was 1.16x on Hyperliquid, 2.87x on Lighter and 6.83x-8.79x on Jupiter Perps, Pacifica and GMTrade; Lighter was 2.4x on 22 November 2026 against a top-ten median of 1.9x, and DefiLlama and CoinMarketCap disagree on its open interest ($538.9M vs $366.6M). Lighter's Robinhood Chain points rules reward volume, positions held and fees paid and exclude standard-to-standard activity; the open-source delta-farmer bot automates delta-neutral hedges across accounts on Lighter on Robinhood Chain, Omni, Pacifica and other exchanges to generate volume and maintain open interest for points programs. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: Tier choice follows strategy type, but the guidance is vendor-side and unmeasured. Lighter's docs call Standard suitable for retail and latency-insensitive traders, Plus for latency-insensitive users who need higher rate limits, and Premium/Advanced for HFT. TrueHold adds that a handful of manual trades a day suits Standard, while traders who take liquidity often in fast markets can lose more than the 0.028% Premium taker fee to 300 ms of slippage, and Plus suits automated strategies that need throughput rather than speed. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: Variational's zero fee is paid through the spread. Omni charges no trading fees and takes its revenue from the spread captured by the Omni Liquidity Provider (OLP). The OLP is a market-making desk run by the founding team that stands opposite all traders and hedges on other venues. The protocol receives a cut of OLP spread revenue instead of a cut of fees. Costs outside the trade price are a flat $0.1 per deposit or withdrawal and a liquidation penalty at ask +0.5% (short) or bid -0.5% (long). (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: In the October 2025 liquidation event, tail losses landed on different parties at Lighter and Hyperliquid. Lighter's LLP lost about 5% (5.35% per Phemex) while Lighter kept providing liquidity instead of using ADL, and an outage lost three transaction batches. Hyperliquid's HLP made over $40 million (Kappa Lab), but Hyperliquid's ADL closed $2.1 billion of positions in 12 minutes. Chitra estimates that profitable traders lost between $45.0M and $51.7M more than the minimum haircut needed to cover the shortfall. Chitra also proves that no ADL policy can satisfy exchange solvency, revenue and fairness at once. Someone pays: LLP depositors on one design, profitable traders on the other. (medium confidence)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: Lighter Standard accounts (the default) pay 0 maker / 0 taker fees on regular perp and spot orders, but pay 1 bp on TWAP/advanced orders and RFQ. The zero fee is not universal across order types. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: Variational's single-dealer design moves the discipline from competition to exit. Critics quoted by Bankless argue a lone dealer means 'one quote with no competition'; OLP's hedging book is not auditable by outsiders; if OLP became insolvent, later accrued profit would be treated as bad debt and not paid out, while user collateral sits in segregated per-user settlement pools. BlockBeats says OLP uses a 'last-look' rejection control (not mentioned on the Variational fee or OLP docs pages read). Variational's trading API was reported as going first to a small group of alpha testers ahead of a public launch. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: During the same event Lighter had an outage: three transaction batches were lost, and security firm Beosin attributed it to dependence on a single sequencer and ZK-proof generation bottlenecks while the CEO admitted a delayed database upgrade (single secondary source, PANews via Phemex). (low confidence)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: A zero fee does not guarantee the cheapest fill at every size: fees dominate small orders and book depth dominates large ones. OpenChainBench states that at $1M notional price impact dwarfs the taker fee, so a zero-fee venue can lose to a 4 bps venue with a deeper book, and that on thin books such as SOL impact can exceed the whole taker fee. It adds that Lighter pays for its 0 bps start with slightly wider spreads on smaller markets. Castle Labs found Hyperliquid had the lowest median slippage at $1M of the five venues it tested on crypto majors: 3.7 bps against 3.8 bps on Binance. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs

text: DefiLlama's fee-summary data for Lighter returns daily fee series and per-product methodology text that says what each line counts; for Lighter, liquidation fees are excluded from revenue and routed to LLP, and supply-side revenue is defined as liquidation fees paid to the LLP. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)
keywords: Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs
